title: Blackened Mahi-Mahi with Lemon Butter Sauce
description: Thermapen-pulled mahi in small oval cast iron pans with a thick lemon-garlic butter sauce that clings.
equipment: Two small oval cast iron pans

ingredients.name: mahi-mahi fillets
ingredients.note: Two even portions, about ¾ inch thick.

steps.title: Mix the mild rub
steps.text: Mix {paprika}, {garlicg}, {onion}, {salt}, {pepper}, {thyme} and {oregano}. Keep {cayenne} aside for the spicy serving.

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.text: Melt {sbutter} in the HexClad. Cook {mgarlic} for 30 seconds, then pour in {broth} and {lemon}. Simmer 2 minutes.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Whisk {cornstarch} with {water}. Stir into the simmering broth for 1 minute until spoon-coating. Stir in {parsley}.

steps.title: Season the fish
steps.text: Brush {fish} with melted {butterdip} and dust with the mild rub. For the spicy option add the reserved cayenne only to that portion.

steps.title: Darken the spices
steps.text: Divide {oil} between the small oval cast iron pans over medium-high heat. Set the seasoned face of each fillet down for 60–90 seconds, just until the spices darken.

steps.title: Finish moist
steps.text: Turn the fillets and lower the heat. Add warm water around the fish to a depth of ¼ inch and cover. Steam 3–7 minutes, until the thickest part reaches 145°F. Spoon hot sauce over each portion.

notes: Make ahead: mix the mild rub ahead and keep the cayenne separate. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes, freeze the cooked fish covered in sauce for up to 1 month; it will flake more easily. Fridge reheat: cover with sauce and warm gently to 165°F. Freezer reheat: thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then reheat covered. Option A uses lemon and the mild spice mix; gentler Option B halves the lemon and leaves out the pepper and cayenne. Use unsalted plant butter for a dairy-free sauce. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 516 kcal, 28.8 g protein, 10.2 g total carbohydrate, 41.0 g fat, 2.7 g fiber, 390 mg sodium.
